# `silk/core/bool`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Named functions for Boolean equality and negation.

## When to use
Use `==`, `!=`, and `!` in ordinary expressions. Use [`equals`](#equals), [`notEquals`](#notEquals), or [`not`](#not) when
the operation must be a named function, such as an argument to a higher-order function.

## Details
These functions return the same results as the operators. They do not allocate and have no
effects.

## Examples
### Compose named Boolean operations
```silk
import silk.core.bool

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let accepted = bool.equals(true, bool.not(false))
  if bool.notEquals(accepted, true) {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `bool` with `import silk.core.bool`.

<a id="equals"></a>

## `equals`

```silk
pub fn equals(left: bool, right: bool) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `left` and `right` have the same value. This function has the same result as
`left == right`.

<a id="notEquals"></a>

## `notEquals`

```silk
pub fn notEquals(left: bool, right: bool) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `left` and `right` have different values. This function has the same result
as `left != right`.

<a id="not"></a>

## `not`

```silk
pub fn not(value: bool) -> bool
```

Returns `false` if `value` is `true`, and `true` if `value` is `false`. This function has the
same result as `!value`.
